newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes sustain gains late on API stock draws.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes sustain gains late on API stock draws.

text.p: U.S. crudes sustained gains in late action Wednesday aided by bullish heating oil and a large draw in crude oil stocks, traders said.
The American Petroleum Institute (API) report showed crude oil stocks fell 6.6 million barrels for the week ended Nov 8.
A draw of 2.88 million barrels in gasoline and 827,000 barrels in heating oil also added to the firm sentiment.
December West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was at $24.20-30 a barrel, up 85 cents from Tuesday's cash market.
The Dec/Jan WTI spread recouped some losses to 15-17 cents a barrel, up from 10-12 cents earlier in the day.
Domestic crude differentials diverged over the busy session, with sweets rallying while sours languished.
A burst of refiner buying helped Light Louisiana Sweet/St James climb to a high of 96 cents a barrel premium over WTI, although it later drifted down to plus 88 cents.
The grade, which was 30 cents weaker last week, was bought heavily by three refiners and some traders, believed to be speculating on the light/heavy spread.
A tight Atlantic arbitrage also helped Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire, which traded at a $1.00 premium to WTI, up from 79 to 85 cents yesterday.
Sour grades, however, continued to weaken hampered by less favorable fundamentals and more sales from the U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR).
West Texas Sour/Midland fell to a low of minus $1.80 a barrel, down from as high as minus $1.61 Tuesday.
The U.S. government sold 2.525 million barrels of oil from the SPR today at an average price of $21.21 a barrel to three refiners, adding to perception of more ample supplies.
Eugene Island traded at minus $1.20-$1.15, up about five cents from Tuesday, but was expected to hold a softer tone.
